stem: A 34-year-old comes in with a productive cough and low-grade evening fevers for about five weeks. They mention a co-worker was treated for 'chest TB' last year but never finished the full course. Exam notes mild crackles at the right apex; the patient's chart also flags recent unexplained weight loss and an old, unrelated shoulder injury that keeps coming up in the history.

patient.social_history: Non-smoker, lives with extended family, shares sleeping quarters with three others
patient.presenting_complaint: Productive cough, low-grade evening fevers, unintentional weight loss
patient.exam_findings: Mild crackles right upper lobe, no lymphadenopathy, BMI 17.8
patient.prior_treatment: None for this episode; reports a co-worker with incomplete prior TB treatment

distractors: Community-acquired bacterial pneumonia not yet resolved
Chronic shoulder-related referred pain being mistaken for chest symptoms
ntep_correct_actions: Order Xpert MTB/RIF or equivalent molecular testing as the initial diagnostic test
Do not wait for smear microscopy before ordering molecular testing where available
who_correct_actions: Order Xpert MTB/RIF or equivalent molecular testing as the initial diagnostic test
Perform rifampicin-resistance detection as part of the same initial molecular test, for every patient
us_correct_actions: Order AFB smear microscopy and both liquid and solid culture in parallel with any NAAT ordered
Do not rely on molecular testing alone to exclude the diagnosis; culture remains the gold standard
critical_error_conditions: Ordering only a chest X-ray with no microbiological confirmation before starting ATT
Treating the shoulder complaint as the primary problem and deferring the respiratory workup
expected_divergence_points: Whether molecular testing alone, or smear-plus-culture, is treated as the mandatory first-line diagnostic step
